sentences.en: This is Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《Hidden Brain》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆（Shankar Vedantam）。

sentences.en: This week for Halloween, the science of fear.
sentences.zh: 本周是万圣节特辑，我们来聊聊恐惧的科学。

sentences.en: We'll talk about what scares us and why sometimes anticipating being afraid
sentences.zh: 我们将探讨是什么让我们感到恐惧，以及为什么有时候对恐惧的预期

sentences.en: can be worse than the thing itself.
sentences.zh: 可能比恐惧本身更糟糕。

sentences.en: Uh, I don't know if I can do this.
sentences.zh: 呃，我不知道我能不能行。

sentences.en: We're going to talk about how changing a few subtle things can make us feel disoriented.
sentences.zh: 我们将讨论一些细微的变化如何让我们感到迷失方向。

sentences.en: Yeah, your body is basically just preparing itself to face whatever
sentences.zh: 没错，你的身体基本上是在为面对即将到来的

sentences.en: it's going to encounter around the next bend.
sentences.zh: 任何事物做准备。

sentences.en: And how this sense of disorientation can increase your fear.
sentences.zh: 以及这种迷失感如何加剧你的恐惧。

sentences.en: Oh my God, what is that?
sentences.zh: 天哪，那是什么？

sentences.en: We'll also explore the upside of fear.
sentences.zh: 我们还将探讨恐惧的积极一面。

sentences.en: Sometimes being scared can actually be a good thing.
sentences.zh: 有时候，感到害怕其实是一件好事。

sentences.en: We're going to do things a little differently in this episode.
sentences.zh: 这一期节目我们会采取一些不同的方式。

sentences.en: We decided to recruit a very brave guinea pig.
sentences.zh: 我们决定招募一只非常勇敢的“小白鼠”。

sentences.en: Oh my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Maggie Penman is one of the producers of this podcaSt.
sentences.zh: 玛吉·彭曼（Maggie Penman）是本节目的制作人之一。

sentences.en: Maggie, welcome.
sentences.zh: 玛吉，欢迎你。

sentences.en: Hi, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 你好，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: I don't sound very brave in that clip, I have to say.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，在那段录音里我听起来一点也不勇敢。

sentences.en: That's not my finest hour.
sentences.zh: 那真是我最丢脸的时刻。

sentences.en: I think you do sound like a guinea pig, though.
sentences.zh: 不过我觉得你听起来确实像只小白鼠。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是。

sentences.en: I sound like I'm being subjected to something, for sure.
sentences.zh: 我敢肯定，我听起来就像正在遭受什么折磨一样。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: You are clearly not someone who enjoys being afraid.
sentences.zh: 显然你不是那种享受恐惧的人。

sentences.en: No, I can't even watch previews for horror movies.
sentences.zh: 没错，我连恐怖片的预告片都不敢看。

sentences.en: So this might explain why over the last few days you have been a little annoyed with me.
sentences.zh: 所以这或许能解释为什么过去几天你对我有点恼火。

sentences.en: So I had this idea that it would be really fun to do an episode about the science of fear for Halloween.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，为万圣节做一期关于恐惧科学的节目应该会很有趣。

sentences.en: And you thought it would be really fun if I went and investigated for myself.
sentences.zh: 而你觉得如果我亲自去调查一下会更有趣。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, what use is a story about fear without somebody who's actually frightened out of their wits?
sentences.zh: 我是说，如果没有一个真正被吓得魂飞魄散的人，关于恐惧的故事还有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: Yeah, I can see why that would be fun for you, but it was slightly less fun for me.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我明白为什么这对你来说很有趣，但对我来说就没那么好玩了。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Tell me what you found.
sentences.zh: 告诉我你发现了什么。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: I drove to Pennsylvania to meet with this woman, Margie Kerr.
sentences.zh: 我开车去了宾夕法尼亚州，去见了一位叫玛吉·克尔（Margie Kerr）的女士。

sentences.en: And she's a sociologist at the University of Pittsburgh.
sentences.zh: 她是匹兹堡大学的一名社会学家。

sentences.en: But she also has this sort of side gig where she curates a haunted house called Scare House and uses it to study fear.
sentences.zh: 但她还有一份“副业”，她策划了一个叫“惊吓屋”（Scare House）的鬼屋，并利用它来研究恐惧。

sentences.en: She actually has a new book out now called Scream, Chilling Adventures in the Science of Fear.
sentences.zh: 她最近刚出版了一本新书，叫《尖叫：恐惧科学中的惊悚冒险》（Scream, Chilling Adventures in the Science of Fear）。

sentences.en: And believe it or not, the cover glows in the dark.
sentences.zh: 而且信不信由你，封面在黑暗中还会发光。

sentences.en: Very unnerving.
sentences.zh: 非常令人不安。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So she's a sociologiSt.
sentences.zh: 所以她是一位社会学家。

sentences.en: She runs a haunted house and she enjoys scaring people out of their wits.
sentences.zh: 她经营着一家鬼屋，还乐于把人吓得魂飞魄散。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So it was funny because Margie was just not what I was expecting.
sentences.zh: 这很有趣，因为玛吉完全不是我预想中的那种人。

sentences.en: She does not look like the kind of person who studies fear for a living.
sentences.zh: 她看起来一点也不像那种以研究恐惧为生的人。

sentences.en: Hi.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Nice to meet you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Come on in.
sentences.zh: 快请进。

sentences.en: She was the sweet, lovely, welcoming person.
sentences.zh: 她是一个甜美、可爱、热情的人。

sentences.en: But every once in a while, she would be describing something in the haunted house and would get really excited about something like this.
sentences.zh: 但每隔一段时间，当她描述鬼屋里的东西时，她就会像这样对某些事物感到非常兴奋。

sentences.en: All of the trick-or-treaters that we've been seeing, all of these very cute kind of cartoonish characters are being decapitated and stabbed and eaten.
sentences.zh: 我们看到的那些“不给糖就捣蛋”的孩子们，所有这些非常可爱、卡通化的角色，都被斩首、刺伤和吃掉了。

sentences.en: Oh, that is just awful, Maggie.
sentences.zh: 哦，那太可怕了，玛吉。

sentences.en: I know.
sentences.zh: 我知道。

sentences.en: So clearly Margie is the kind of person who loves this stuff.
sentences.zh: 很明显，玛吉就是那种热爱这些东西的人。

sentences.en: She loves horror movies.
sentences.zh: 她热爱恐怖电影。

sentences.en: She's always loved creepy, crawly monsters.
sentences.zh: 她一直都很喜欢那些毛骨悚然的怪物。

sentences.en: It's just kind of like her thing.
sentences.zh: 这就像是她的个人爱好。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Mental note to self.
sentences.zh: 心里记下一笔。

sentences.en: Avoid Margie Kerr on quiet streets, especially late at night.
sentences.zh: 在安静的街道上，尤其是在深夜，要避开玛吉·克尔。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: No, but seriously, she was lovely.
sentences.zh: 不，说真的，她人很好。

sentences.en: I met with her on a Saturday afternoon.
sentences.zh: 我是周六下午见到她的。

sentences.en: I got a tour of her lab.
sentences.zh: 我参观了她的实验室。

sentences.en: We had this great chat about fear and science, what makes horror movies so popular.
sentences.zh: 我们关于恐惧和科学，以及为什么恐怖电影如此受欢迎进行了很棒的交谈。

sentences.en: And then I came back at night.
sentences.zh: 然后我晚上又去了。

sentences.en: This is the part of the tape where you're going to hear my voice get about an octave higher.
sentences.zh: 录音里的这一部分，你会听到我的声音高了大约一个八度。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: So I'm imagining that this is because you're afraid, your muscles are tensing up, your vocal cords are going to get clenched,
sentences.zh: 我想这是因为你感到害怕，肌肉变得紧张，声带收紧，

sentences.en: and that's why you're going to sound like a guinea pig.
sentences.zh: 所以你听起来才像只小白鼠。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, that all sounds very scientific.
sentences.zh: 我是说，这听起来确实很科学。

sentences.en: I think my experience was just sort of like low-grade panic attack for about 25 minutes.
sentences.zh: 我觉得我的经历就像是持续了25分钟的轻度恐慌发作。

sentences.en: So whatever floats your boat.
sentences.zh: 随你怎么说吧。

sentences.en: So, but you're going to hear another voice in this tape, too, and that was Margie falling behind me collecting data.
sentences.zh: 不过，在这段录音里你还会听到另一个声音，那是玛吉跟在我后面收集数据。

sentences.en: And then I was also wearing this crazy lab coat with, like, little things stuck on my fingers and torso collecting my heart rate and something called galvanic skin response,
sentences.zh: 我当时还穿着一件奇怪的实验服，手指和躯干上贴着小东西，用来收集我的心率和一种叫“皮肤电反应”的数据，

sentences.en: which is basically just how sweaty someone is getting.
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是测量一个人出汗的程度。

sentences.en: And they use that as a measurement for how scared you are.
sentences.zh: 他们用这个来衡量你有多害怕。

sentences.en: So I want to hear what the data was, but before that, Margie, just tell me a little bit about the house.
sentences.zh: 我想听听数据结果，但在此之前，玛吉，先给我简单介绍一下这个鬼屋吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the beginning of the haunted house incorporated a lot of the building's history, which was really cool.
sentences.zh: 鬼屋的开头融入了很多建筑的历史，这真的很酷。

sentences.en: So this building used to be the Elks Club Lodge, and it has this sort of faded glamour.
sentences.zh: 这座建筑以前是麋鹿俱乐部（Elks Club Lodge），有一种褪色的魅力。

sentences.en: There's this spooky 1920s music kind of coming through an old phonograph.
sentences.zh: 留声机里传出那种诡异的20世纪20年代的音乐。

sentences.en: It sounds almost underwater.
sentences.zh: 听起来几乎像是从水下传来的。

sentences.en: There's a party scene.
sentences.zh: 里面有一个派对场景。

sentences.en: It's full of people and animatronics and dolls in costumes.
sentences.zh: 到处都是人、电动玩偶和穿着戏服的假人。

sentences.en: And one of the very creepy things about this is you're never quite sure which one you're dealing with until you're very close.
sentences.zh: 最诡异的一点是，在走近之前，你永远无法确定你面对的到底是人还是玩偶。

sentences.en: Oh, my God.
sentences.zh: 天哪。

sentences.en: Lots of taxidermy on the walls.
sentences.zh: 墙上挂着很多动物标本。

sentences.en: And then it went from creepy to brutal with some human taxidermy.
sentences.zh: 然后场景从诡异变成了残酷，出现了一些人体标本。

sentences.en: What did you just say?
sentences.zh: 你刚才说什么？

sentences.en: Human taxidermy.
sentences.zh: 人体标本。

sentences.en: They were actually stuffing human beings?
sentences.zh: 他们真的在填充人类尸体吗？

sentences.en: Well, that looked like the plan.
sentences.zh: 嗯，看起来确实是那个计划。

sentences.en: There were some sort of mangled bodies hanging from the ceiling, blood, gore.
sentences.zh: 天花板上挂着一些残缺不全的尸体，到处是血和内脏。

sentences.en: Or, yeah, this is where I sort of started to freak out.
sentences.zh: 或者说，这就是我开始崩溃的地方。

sentences.en: Uh, I don't know if I can do this.
sentences.zh: 呃，我不知道我能不能行。

sentences.en: You can do it!
sentences.zh: 你可以的！

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: I love the fact that she's encouraging you, that she's goading you on.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢她鼓励你、怂恿你的样子。

sentences.en: I love that.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个。

sentences.en: She's very gleeful about her work.
sentences.zh: 她对自己的工作感到非常愉悦。

sentences.en: That's what I'll say.
sentences.zh: 我只能这么说。

sentences.en: And throughout the whole house, there's this kind of creepy soundtrack of whispers and music.
sentences.zh: 整个鬼屋里都回荡着那种诡异的低语和音乐声。

sentences.en: And then, of course, there are the actors.
sentences.zh: 当然，还有那些演员。

sentences.en: Oh!
sentences.zh: 哦！

sentences.en: Are you the chosen one?
sentences.zh: 你是那个被选中的人吗？

sentences.en: Well, this guy was sort of like half-human and he was just getting all up in my space.
sentences.zh: 这个家伙半人半鬼的，一直往我身边凑。

sentences.en: Oh, I can smell it.
sentences.zh: 哦，我闻到了。

sentences.en: Let me see.
sentences.zh: 让我看看。

sentences.en: Oh, yes.
sentences.zh: 哦，是的。

sentences.en: Follow me.
sentences.zh: 跟我来。

sentences.en: All right, that sounds really creepy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，那听起来真的很诡异。

sentences.en: Okay, see?
sentences.zh: 你看，明白了吗？

sentences.en: This isn't kid stuff.
sentences.zh: 这可不是小孩子的把戏。

sentences.en: I am so sorry I did this to you, Maggie.
sentences.zh: 玛吉，我真的很抱歉让你经历这些。

sentences.en: Oh, well, it's okay.
sentences.zh: 哦，没关系。

sentences.en: We're going to bring it up with the union, but in the meantime.
sentences.zh: 我们会向工会反映这件事的，但在此之前……

sentences.en: So, yeah, there are a lot of what Margie referred to as boo scares, which is basically something
sentences.zh: 所以，没错，有很多玛吉所说的“跳跃式惊吓”（boo scares），基本上就是某样东西

sentences.en: or someone jumping out and surprising you.
sentences.zh: 或某个人突然跳出来吓你一跳。

sentences.en: Are we ready?
sentences.zh: 准备好了吗？

sentences.en: Leading to reactions like that.
sentences.zh: 导致了那样的反应。

sentences.en: Crack your head.
sentences.zh: 把你的头敲碎。

sentences.en: This way.
sentences.zh: 这边走。

sentences.en: You know, that's interesting, Maggie, because when I think of scary stuff, I really divide
sentences.zh: 你知道吗，这很有趣，玛吉，因为当我想到恐怖的东西时，我真的会把它

sentences.en: it into two kinds of things in my head.
sentences.zh: 在脑海里分成两类。

sentences.en: So there's the scary stuff like we just heard, where something jumps out at you and makes
sentences.zh: 一类就是我们刚才听到的那种，某样东西突然跳出来，发出

sentences.en: a scary sound.
sentences.zh: 可怕的声音。

sentences.en: And there's also the other kind of scary stuff, where the fear sort of builds up really, really
sentences.zh: 还有另一种恐怖，恐惧感会非常、非常缓慢地积累，

sentences.en: slowly, and you know that something bad is going to happen, but you just don't know
sentences.zh: 你知道会有坏事发生，但你就是不知道

sentences.en: when.
sentences.zh: 什么时候发生。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And it's funny because the boo scares are actually pretty light.
sentences.zh: 有趣的是，跳跃式惊吓其实相当轻微。

sentences.en: Even though I was screaming, you can hear Margie sort of laughing at herself in the background
sentences.zh: 尽管我在尖叫，但你可以在背景音里听到玛吉因为被吓到而自嘲的笑声。

sentences.en: for being startled.
sentences.zh: 大多数自愿走进鬼屋的人都会有这种反应。

sentences.en: And most people who voluntarily go through a haunted house have that reaction.
sentences.zh: 但真正令人不安的是那些细微的东西，比如扭曲的镜子、黑暗、

sentences.en: But what was really unnerving was the subtle stuff, the sort of distorted mirrors and darkness
sentences.zh: 雾气和噪音。

sentences.en: and fog and noise.
sentences.zh: 我不知道我该往哪边走。

sentences.en: I don't know which way I'm supposed to be going.
sentences.zh: 是的，从这边走。

sentences.en: Yes, we're through here.
sentences.zh: 天哪，我真的能听出你声音里的恐慌。

sentences.en: Oh my gosh, I can really hear the panic in your voice there.
sentences.zh: 没错，那种迷失方向的感觉真的让我崩溃了。

sentences.en: Yeah, the disorientation stuff really freaked me out.
sentences.zh: 有些房间完全是黑的。

sentences.en: And some of the rooms were completely dark.
sentences.zh: 你必须摸索着前进，不知道下一个转角会有什么。

sentences.en: You had to sort of feel your way through, not knowing what might be around the next corner.
sentences.zh: 我们走出鬼屋后，我确实和玛吉谈过那种感觉。

sentences.en: I actually talked to Margie about that sensation after we got out of the house.
sentences.zh: 没错，全黑的房间太可怕了，因为我们无法利用任何东西来判断

sentences.en: Yeah, the blackout rooms are so terrifying because we can't use anything to sort of gauge
sentences.zh: 我们在空间中的位置。

sentences.en: our position in space.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So our proprioception is completely out of whack because we really need just something,
sentences.zh: 我们的本体感觉完全失调了，因为我们确实需要一些东西，

sentences.en: just even the slightest little light to kind of give us an idea of what's up and what's
sentences.zh: 哪怕是最微弱的一点光，来让我们知道什么是上，什么是

sentences.en: down.
sentences.zh: 下。

sentences.en: And when you take that away through darkness or, you know, with the use of fog, there's
sentences.zh: 而当你通过黑暗，或者你知道的，利用雾气把这些剥夺时，

sentences.en: a ton of fog.
sentences.zh: 那里有大量的雾。

sentences.en: Strobe lights too.
sentences.zh: 还有频闪灯。

sentences.en: Strobe lights combined with hyperventilation are the best at inducing a feeling of depersonalization
sentences.zh: 频闪灯结合过度换气，最能诱发一种人格解体感，

sentences.en: or when you sort of feel like you're outside of yourself.
sentences.zh: 或者说让你感觉自己仿佛置身于躯体之外。

sentences.en: So here's what I'm thinking, Maggie, and I'm actually thinking about something much more
sentences.zh: 所以我是这么想的，玛吉，而且此时此刻，我考虑的事情比鬼屋要

sentences.en: serious than haunted houses at this point.
sentences.zh: 严肃得多。

sentences.en: The whole thing that she just talked about, the idea of disorientation and triggering disorientation
sentences.zh: 她刚才谈到的整件事，关于迷失方向以及通过触发迷失方向

sentences.en: as a way to trigger fear, I feel like psychologists have actually applied this in all kinds of
sentences.zh: 来引发恐惧的理念，我觉得心理学家们实际上已经以各种方式应用了这一点，

sentences.en: ways, some of which are actually quite unethical.
sentences.zh: 其中一些方式其实相当不道德。

sentences.en: If you look at the ways in which people have practiced torture, people have used exactly
sentences.zh: 如果你看看人们实施酷刑的方式，他们使用的正是

sentences.en: the same techniques of using strobe lights and loud music, darkness, cold, sounds of crying
sentences.zh: 同样的技巧，利用频闪灯、大声的音乐、黑暗、寒冷、婴儿的

sentences.en: babies.
sentences.zh: 哭声。

sentences.en: And when you pipe these things in to people over extended periods of time, it actually
sentences.zh: 当你长时间地向人们灌输这些东西时，它实际上

sentences.en: is as traumatic as actually being beaten or abused or being physically violated in some
sentences.zh: 和遭受殴打、虐待或以某种方式受到身体侵害一样，

sentences.en: way.
sentences.zh: 具有创伤性。

sentences.en: I can really imagine that because even though this was a haunted house, it was a very controlled
sentences.zh: 我真的能想象，因为尽管这是一个鬼屋，但它是一个非常受控的

sentences.en: environment.
sentences.zh: 环境。

sentences.en: I knew I was safe the whole time.
sentences.zh: 我全程都知道自己是安全的。

sentences.en: There is just something so disorienting about being in a completely dark room or being constantly

sentences.en: He's a senior producer at Morning Edition and also a magician, and he's been on this
sentences.zh: 他是《早间新闻》的资深制作人，也是一位魔术师，他之前也上过

sentences.en: program before.
sentences.zh: 这个节目。

sentences.en: Welcome, Barry.
sentences.zh: 欢迎你，巴里。

sentences.en: Thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: I'm looking forward to intimidating you.
sentences.zh: 我很期待能吓唬吓唬你。

sentences.en: You have long played the muscle in many experiments.
sentences.zh: 你曾在许多实验中长期扮演“打手”的角色。

sentences.en: Yes, and look at that bicep.
sentences.zh: 没错，看看那肱二头肌。

sentences.en: It's pretty impressive, yes.
sentences.zh: 确实令人印象深刻。

sentences.en: What are we going to do, Barry?
sentences.zh: 我们要怎么做，巴里？

sentences.en: Shankar, I have with me an envelope that I'd like to give to you.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，我这里有个信封想交给你。

sentences.en: Thank you, Barry.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，巴里。

sentences.en: What does the envelope say?
sentences.zh: 信封上写着什么？

sentences.en: The envelope has the word prediction written in a red felt pen.
sentences.zh: 信封上用红色记号笔写着“预测”二字。

sentences.en: Yes, and we're going to do it with a deck of cards.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们要用一副扑克牌来完成它。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: What I want you to do is pick the card that has been predicted in that envelope.
sentences.zh: 我要你选出信封里预测的那张牌。

sentences.en: There's only a small problem, Barry.
sentences.zh: 有个小问题，巴里。

sentences.en: I don't know what card has been predicted in the envelope.
sentences.zh: 我不知道信封里预测的是哪张牌。

sentences.en: Well, that's because you don't have the proper motivation.
sentences.zh: 嗯，那是因为你缺乏足够的动力。

sentences.en: What we have to do is put your mind in the right place so you can concentrate and use your
sentences.zh: 我们要做的是让你的大脑进入正确的状态，这样你才能集中注意力，发挥你

sentences.en: superior mental abilities.
sentences.zh: 卓越的思维能力。

sentences.en: What do you have in mind?
sentences.zh: 你有什么打算？

sentences.en: I have here a plate and a can of whipped cream.
sentences.zh: 我这里有一个盘子和一罐鲜奶油。

sentences.en: What are you doing here, Barry?
sentences.zh: 你在干什么，巴里？

sentences.en: Barry, what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 巴里，你在做什么？

sentences.en: Well, the idea is very simple.
sentences.zh: 嗯，这个想法很简单。

sentences.en: Should you fail in this task, it will be Maggie's job to hit you in the face with this
sentences.zh: 如果你在这个任务中失败了，玛吉的任务就是用这个

sentences.en: whipped cream pie.
sentences.zh: 鲜奶油派砸你的脸。

sentences.en: Maggie, you are not going to do that.
sentences.zh: 玛吉，你可不能那样做。

sentences.en: Well, I don't know, Shankar.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我不知道，尚卡尔。

sentences.en: You heard me in that haunted house.
sentences.zh: 你在鬼屋里听到了我的尖叫。

sentences.en: I'm a little upset right now, so...
sentences.zh: 我现在有点心烦意乱，所以……

sentences.en: I have to say, I feel extremely focused right now.
sentences.zh: 我不得不说，我现在感觉极其专注。

sentences.en: Very good.
sentences.zh: 非常好。

sentences.en: But actually, let me help your decision process a little bit.
sentences.zh: 但其实，让我来帮你加速一下决策过程吧。

sentences.en: May I have five seconds on the clock, please?
sentences.zh: 能给我五秒钟倒计时吗？

sentences.en: Oh, dear.
sentences.zh: 哦，天哪。

sentences.en: That's the one right there?
sentences.zh: 就是那一张吗？

sentences.en: Yes, that's the one right there.
sentences.zh: 是的，就是那一张。

sentences.en: Okay, keep your finger on the card.
sentences.zh: 好的，把你的手指按在那张牌上。

sentences.en: All right, so I picked a card.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我选了一张牌。

sentences.en: So, Maggie, I would really appreciate it if you didn't bring the plate so close.
sentences.zh: 那么，玛吉，如果你能别把盘子靠得那么近，我会非常感激的。

sentences.en: Shankar, will you open the envelope, please?
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，请打开信封好吗？

sentences.en: All right, I'm extracting a sheet of paper that was in the envelope, and it says, Shankar
sentences.zh: 好的，我正在取出信封里的一张纸，上面写着：尚卡尔

sentences.en: will pick the eight of hearts.
sentences.zh: 会选红桃8。

sentences.en: Now, let's see if it matches the card you picked.
sentences.zh: 现在，让我们看看它是否和你选的牌一致。

sentences.en: Maggie, stand by with the pie.
sentences.zh: 玛吉，准备好派。

sentences.en: Shankar, turn over the card.
sentences.zh: 尚卡尔，翻开那张牌。

sentences.en: Oh, no!
sentences.zh: 哦，不！

sentences.en: It's the eight of hearts.
sentences.zh: 是红桃8。

sentences.en: Bummer.
sentences.zh: 真倒霉。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: How did I pick this card, Barry?
sentences.zh: 我是怎么选到这张牌的，巴里？

sentences.en: First of all, sorry to disappoint you, Maggie.
sentences.zh: 首先，很抱歉让你失望了，玛吉。

sentences.en: I was really looking forward to that.
sentences.zh: 我本来很期待那一幕的。

sentences.en: The reason you picked the card is you fell into my little trap.
sentences.zh: 你选到这张牌的原因是你掉进了我的小陷阱。

sentences.en: I used fear to cloud your judgment just a little bit.
sentences.zh: 我利用恐惧稍微干扰了你的判断力。

sentences.en: And you're saying that somehow shaped which card I picked?
sentences.zh: 你是说这在某种程度上影响了我选哪张牌？

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: If I could introduce a little bit of tension into the moment with the pie and also with
sentences.zh: 如果我能通过派和倒计时给当下制造一点紧张感，那就会抑制你进行分析选择的能力，并迫使

sentences.en: the deadline clock, that would inhibit your ability to make an analytical choice and force
sentences.zh: 你做出仓促的决定，从而大大增加我的魔术成功的几率。

sentences.en: you into a snap decision that greatly increases the odds that my trick will succeed.
sentences.zh: 所以，巴里，我觉得这最迷人的地方在于，我觉得同样的事情

sentences.en: So what I find really fascinating about this, Barry, is that I feel like the same thing
sentences.zh: 也发生在你身上，玛吉，当你在鬼屋的时候。

sentences.en: happened to you, Maggie, when you were at Scare House.
sentences.zh: 你的批判性思维能力直接关闭了。

sentences.en: Your critical thinking skills just simply shut down.
sentences.zh: 是的，这正是玛吉告诉我们的。

sentences.en: Yeah, this is exactly what Margie was telling us about.
sentences.zh: 去鬼屋实际上能让人感觉更好，因为他们不再

sentences.en: It actually makes people feel better to go through a haunted house because they can't
sentences.zh: 去想那些让他们烦恼的事情了。

sentences.en: think about the things they've been worrying about anymore.
sentences.zh: 我不能说我现在感觉好多了，但巴里，谢谢你为我们展示那个魔术。

sentences.en: I can't say I feel better already, but Barry, thank you for showing us that magic trick.
sentences.zh: 如果你脸上沾着奶油派，我会感觉更好些。

sentences.en: I'd feel better if you were wearing that cream pie.
sentences.zh: 如果是我在吃那个奶油派，我会感觉更好些。

sentences.en: I'd feel better if I were eating the cream pie.
